name: Organization service accounts

contract.identity: Dedicated organization machine records with a currently eligible responsible human; no human passwords, browser sessions or approval votes.
contract.administration: Current owner/admin human browser session, CSRF and recent actual signed passkey/MFA required for every write, including at the transaction boundary.
contract.credential: One independent organization project; explicit read plus supported logs/deploy/rollback/jobs/secrets/audit; 5-minute to 30-day expiry; dedicated clsa_ prefix; exact current hash, grant, owner, generation and lifecycle guards.
contract.rotation: Versioned rotation, disable and owner transfer atomically revoke preceding keys. Ineligible owners do not prevent emergency disable. Re-enabling never revives old keys.
contract.recovery: Bounded encrypted actor/organization exact receipts return the originally issued key after interrupted delivery. Historical acknowledgements cannot revive later disabled or rotated authority. Audits and effects share control-store transactions.
contract.attribution: Native audit metadata identifies machine account, credential and generation. Authenticated-attempt counters include subsequently rejected operations. Existing agent budget grants/debits identify the organization owner and distinct machine principal. Native project resource usage remains aggregate, not per-key invoices.
contract.server: authenticateServiceAccount(request) returns a frozen server capability with current-authority closure. JSON metadata cannot authenticate a caller. Separate application/control stores and providers do not become a distributed transaction.
contract.compatibility: Opt-in additive protocol1 tables; no extra NPM dependencies. Unknown protocol refuses startup/current operations. Preserve the master key and matching control-store backup; rollback cannot certify newer protocols or reactivate old prefix credentials.

nativeEvidence: Real AuthServer signed UV passkey step-up; password-only administration refused. Only enrolled public key is seeded, not session authentication flags.
Real held HTTP machine upload rotates its credential before remaining body; 401, zero guarded secret/audit effects.
Real native controller SIGKILL after credential commit before HTTP delivery; restart replays one encrypted exact key, and later disable remains current.
Two native HTTP controllers race the same expected version: one accepted rotation, one conflict, one current generation.
Strict project selection, explicit logs scope, human-only administration, machine audit/counters, owner loss and expiry.
Trusted machine caller executes one accepted agent budget mutation; exact retry spends once and rotation rejects the old caller; management requires an independent capability.
Protocol rejection, rollback on failed audit, caps, stale versions, encrypted restart receipts and emergency disable.
